### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a8396da1589d77496418a77d96f3ee73873893a5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9259ad978b75332791b13dd95626942170253d0f` — the merge of head `1782a6175b0091d213cbb1ea27c65a19b6c8b8e3` into base `a8396da1589d77496418a77d96f3ee73873893a5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9259ad978b75332791b13dd95626942170253d0f && git checkout 9259ad978b75332791b13dd95626942170253d0f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a8396da1589d77496418a77d96f3ee73873893a5 1782a6175b0091d213cbb1ea27c65a19b6c8b8e3 && git checkout -B drift-repro a8396da1589d77496418a77d96f3ee73873893a5 && git merge --no-ff 1782a6175b0091d213cbb1ea27c65a19b6c8b8e3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a8396da1589d77496418a77d96f3ee73873893a5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对 — L1 REWORK @ `a7ed93d6324cf6798967a8b0feffc81cd211d004`

**Verdict: REWORK**, on L1 findings I read in the tree myself. **No contract record is posted for this head.** The isolated reviewer run claimed at 7215644764 fell off `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` partway through (`verify-review-tier` refused it), so it counts for nothing. A fresh at-tier review runs on the fix head. CI was still running at this reading (24 runs pending).

### What to change

1. **R1 (must-fix): the "no position" preview promises an exemption the gate does not give.**
   - **What it says.** `view.switcher.audienceNoPosition` (all 11 locales) and `engine.form.audienceNoPosition` (studio en / zh) read "only people granted them directly, **and the object's editors**, will see this view / it". The module header of `capabilityAudience.ts` says the same: "a misspelled gate hides the view from everyone but the object's editors".
   - **Why it is false.** Both surfaces write carriers the read gate refuses whole, to an author as to anyone: the create card writes a view item, and the Studio row edits a view item or a dashboard (`meta-item-read-gate.ts`, the view and dashboard arms, as PR 1's hint now says). The editor exemption belongs only to an object's own `listViews` (ADR-0106 D4), and neither surface writes that.
   - **Why it matters.** The sentence errs in the lockout direction, and in Studio it contradicts the row hint just above it.
   - **The fix.** Drop the editor clause in every copy, the header and the pin.
2. **R2 (should-fix): the create card never tells its creator the gate applies to them.**
   - The card's strings (`audienceLabel` … `audiencePositionsUnread`) carry no self-refusal sentence. Only the Studio row hint and `capabilities.mdx` say it.
   - The card is where a creator can pick a capability they do not hold, and after Create the flow opens the view they can no longer read.
   - Say it on the card, or mark the creator's own reach in the preview.
3. **R3 (should-fix): the position preview recomputes what the server already serves.**
   - `capabilityAudience.ts` joins raw `position.permissionSets` with raw permission-set bodies in the browser. Its own caveat admits it "does not read the activation ledger".
   - `GET /meta/position?include=grants`, which `PositionGrantCells.tsx` already reads, answers each position's sets in force.
   - Prime Directive 5 asks for the served answer, or a stated reason not to use it. As written, the preview over-reports who will see the view.
4. **R4 (should-fix): the Studio picker is not what its docblock and `capabilities.mdx` describe.**
   - `CapabilityAudienceFooter` draws positions only, never the granting sets.
   - `RefMultiWidget` keeps its free-text arm when the catalog is unread or empty, so "you cannot type a name that matches nothing" is not true there.
   - Make the widget match the words, or the words match the widget.

These move code, so the round's head gets the at-tier review (schema face: `view.metadata-form.ts`, `dashboard.metadata-form.ts`, plus the picker that implements their row) before an ACCEPT.

### Read and clean at this head

- **Shape** (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37906`): open, draft, base `main`. It is the card's second PR, after #37839. Declarations are `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, with four packages at `patch`.
- **The dev's footer nit:** no PR-body guard reads the `_Generated by …_` line, and I found none in `scripts/` or `.github/workflows/`. The session attribution footer is fine.
- **Still owed:** green CI, and a sentence-by-sentence read of `.changeset/34908-view-audience-picker.md` and `capabilities.mdx`. I read those on the fix head, since R1–R4 change what they describe.

2026-11-27T11:58Z — fix head for the L1 REWORK (comment 7215827467): `9731b21d76`. Three commits on top of `a7ed93d632`, no rebase.

- **R1.** The editor clause is gone from every copy: `view.switcher.audienceNoPosition` (all 11 locales, zh-Hant regenerated by `gen-zh-hant.mjs`), `engine.form.audienceNoPosition` (studio en / zh) and the `capabilityAudience.ts` header ("hides the view, or the dashboard, from everyone, its author included"). The pin now reads "only people granted them directly will see …".
- **R2.** While a gate is picked, the create card says it applies to its creator: `view.switcher.audienceSelf`, "This applies to you too: if you do not hold every capability picked, the view leaves your own list once it is created" (testid `view-audience-self`).
- **R3.** The preview reads the served answer: `list('position', { include: 'grants' })` and each row's `_grantedPermissionSets`, the sets in force. Raw `permissionSets` are never joined. A list served without the decoration leaves the positions unknown (`null`), like a failed read. Pinned: a switched-off position (grants `[]`) reaches no one, and a raw set name that is not served is ignored.
- **R4.** The Studio widget now matches the words. `ref-multi:capability` is a closed registry: no typed-name box when the catalog is unread, empty or failed. Each offered option shows "Granted by …" (testid `ref-multi-capability-detail`). The changeset, the `view.metadata-form.ts` comment and `capabilities.mdx` say the same.
- **CI fix (new in `2156f1acc8`).** At `f67c1e60c5`, Test UI 6/16 failed on the network-escape guard. `DashboardDefaultInspector`, `ViewVariantInspector` and `ResourceEditPage` read the three registries on mount, so `DashboardDefaultInspector.layoutColumns-11796` and `AddWidgetPicker.oneRegistry-26745` reached `/meta/capability`. The hosts now hand a stable loader down (`WidgetContext.loadCapabilityAudience`, `useCapabilityAudienceLoader`), and the picker reads it once its row is on screen, so a closed Access section sends no request. A catalog the host already holds still wins. Two new cases pin this: no request until the collapsed section opens, then exactly one; and no loader call when a catalog is given.

Measured at this head:
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: 114 derived, 114 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. All 114 exited 0. Six spec gates first answered exit 3 on a stale dts; they were re-run after a spec rebuild and exited 0.
- The changeset-only last commit re-derives the same 114. Its three changeset gates exit 0.
- ui, 5 files, 135 tests passed: `viewAudience-34908`, `SchemaForm.widgetLabelling`, the two files that escaped, and `WidgetContext.catalogUnion`.
- app-shell `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 0.
- CI at `2156f1acc8`: 61 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed.

For the body (the seat's to patch): the Studio paragraph's "load the catalog (`useCapabilityAudienceLoad`) only when the form on screen declares the widget" is now "hand down a loader (`useCapabilityAudienceLoader`); the picker reads it once its row is on screen". The Tests block's head and counts are as above.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9731b21d769043d6b399a68a8089c750376f7b79`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.metadata-form.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.metadata-form.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/capabilityAudience.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ViewAudiencePicker.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/CreateViewDialog.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewViewCrud.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewTitleSwitcher.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/useCapabilityAudienceLoader.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ViewVariantInspector.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/DashboardDefaultInspector.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/metadata-form-zh-cn.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/zh-Hans.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/en.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/zh.ts

Full review, not a delta: no `## Contract review` record exists for this PR on any head (the run claimed at 7215644764 fell off tier and posted nothing).

Inputs read: card #34908 (body and all seven comments: triage 6953426292, split 7016189680, analysis 7098042572, ruling 7103739693, claim 7210714615, dev report 7215584003); PR #37906 (body, the 49-file list, the net diff against `main` at `2a4ad3043c70ba29453eae87b97b4ab0e019eee4`; the compare API answers `ahead 4, behind 0` with that commit as merge base, so the head carries no stale base); its comments (L1 REWORK 7215827467 with R1 to R4, the fix note 7217699980, both review claims); PR #37839 with its three contract records (7211660535, 7212800744, 7213693656) for the vocabulary and the nits N2 to N5; and the check-runs on this head.

Check-runs on this head when read: completed `success` for Auto Label, Check Changeset (one of its two runs), Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, both PR-body guards runs, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates and filter; 11 `skipped` (opt-in and schedule jobs); none failed. STILL PENDING, so not judged here: Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, the second Check Changeset run, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace. No Test UI shard had been created yet. This reading of the tree does not stand in for those conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

- `viewForm` and `dashboardForm`: the `requiredPermissions` row's `widget` moves from `string-tags` to `ref-multi:capability`. RIGHT. `widget` is a free string on the form spec (the sibling `ref-multi:permission` sits in `position.metadata-form.ts:34` with no spec-side vocabulary), so no accept-set moves; the value the row writes is still a list of names into the same key, at the same position the read gate asks (`filterViewForUser`, `meta-item-read-gate.ts:947-968`, and the dashboard arm at `:1826-1829`).
- The view hint's last sentence changes from "you can no longer open this view either" to "you no longer see this view in the list either". RIGHT, and it closes N5 of #37839: every carrier this row can write is a `view` document, where a view item is refused whole to its author and a container's `list` / `listViews` entry is pruned for a non-holder on the plain read (`filterViewForUser`), so the switcher drops it for the person setting the gate on each. An object's own `listViews` (served to the object's editors, ADR-0106 D4) is not written through this form. The dashboard hint is unchanged and still exact ("refused WHOLE … author or not").
- No schema key, accepted value, gate, export barrel or `*.zod.ts` is touched; the ruled "no new key, no new gate, no any-of form" holds on the diff. RIGHT.
- New optional members on `WidgetContext` (`capabilityAudience`, `loadCapabilityAudience`), `InPlaceViewRequest.requiredPermissions`, `CreateViewCardProps.loadAudience` / `initialRequiredPermissions`, one `WIDGETS` registration with its `WIDGET_LABELLING` row, and 13 console plus 10 Studio i18n keys. RIGHT as additive; every existing caller compiles unchanged, and a host that hands no loader gets a closed picker that says so, never a crash.
- Behaviour change in the create door: a new shared view used to inherit the open view's gate silently; with the picker offered the pick is authoritative and an empty pick writes no key (`objectViewViewCrud.tsx`, the `if (requiredPermissions)` arm). RIGHT: the inherited gate is shown as the starting value, so nothing is dropped unseen, and without a picker the body is built as before.
- The generated `metadataForms` bundles and source hashes follow from the one changed leaf. RIGHT as a derivation; their content is the lane seat's.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/34908-view-audience-picker.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in the changeset body and the PR body. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: nothing a metadata author can write changes, and `none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). The four packages are the four released packages the diff moves. `Clause-②: no` holds on my reading: no accept or reject behaviour of any contract changes, and what is added is optional props on console components and catalog strings, not a served or authorable surface. One `Check Changeset` run concluded `success`; the second was pending. Each changeset sentence was read against the tree and agrees with it, including "a list served without them leaves the positions unknown" and "no typed-name box when the catalog is unread, empty or failed".

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation "the ruling's `studio-design/ObjectListViewInspector.tsx` is gone from `main`": ANSWERED, as in #37839. The picker lands in `ViewVariantInspector.tsx` through the form row, which is the Studio view panel today.
- Dev deviation "Studio `ref-multi:capability` keeps the typed-name box when no catalog is fed": STALE and now false in the right direction; R4 closed it and `RefMultiWidget`'s `registry.closed` arm renders no input on any arm. The report line predates the fix head.
- Dev deviation "`DashboardDefaultInspector` now passes a `WidgetContext` with `conditionScopeForMetadataType('dashboard')`": ANSWERED. `dashboardForm` declares no `condition` row, and `DashboardInPageEditor` mounts the same inspector, so the in-page editor gets the loader too and no host of `dashboardForm` is left with an unfed closed picker.
- The analysis's first confidence gap ("whether the console can already read the capability catalog and the position to permission-set map"): ANSWERED on `main`, no new read was needed. `GET /meta/capability` and `GET /meta/permission` are already read by `preview/capabilityLint.ts:116-137` with the same row unwrapping and the same `systemPermissions` key; `MetadataClient.list` accepts `include: 'grants'` (`metadata-client.ts:270-275`, `:1249-1252`); the server step is `describeMetaPositionList` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:4657-4680`), which serves `_grantedPermissionSets` as a list of `{ name, via }`, the shape `grantedSetsOf` reads. An undecorated row (no service, anonymous) leaves it absent and the code answers "unknown", as the server's own docblock requires.
- `open_questions`: none declared.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no server join. The position to set edge is the server's answer, read where the resolver enforces it (R3 of the L1). What remains in the browser is a join of two metadata registry lists (set to capability, capability to granting sets), which has no SQL shape and no served equivalent. Nothing to find.

### ④ Design judgment

`view.metadata-form.ts` and `dashboard.metadata-form.ts`, against ruling 7103739693 (letter B), step 2 of the execution in 7098042572, the gate they describe and their consumers; then each implementing file against those rows, sentence by sentence.

What holds:
- Closed list. The create card has no input at all; the Studio widget's `closed` arm shows a notice (unread, none, failed) or a disabled trigger (loading). A stored name the catalog does not know stays listed and flagged, never dropped. The offered names are declared capabilities plus every name a set grants, which is the ruled "capabilities the environment knows".
- "Granting stays in Setup": no write to a permission set or a position anywhere in the diff.
- The preview is the all-of reading of `holdsRequiredPermissions` per position, over sets in force; a switched-off position reaches no one; an unread or undecorated position list says "could not be read" and never guesses.
- Lazy read: the card reads only once Shared is picked; the Studio row reads on mount of the row, so a collapsed section sends nothing; a catalog the host already holds wins.
- R1 is gone from all eleven console locales, both Studio namespaces and the module header; R2's self-refusal line is on the card in all eleven; each was read.
- `capabilities.mdx`: the recipe, the "switched off reaches no one" sentence and the warning callout each match the gate and the code.

Tried to break it:

S1 (should-fix) — the "no position" preview states an exclusive audience that the resolver does not enforce. `view.switcher.audienceNoPosition` (eleven locales) and `engine.form.audienceNoPosition` (Studio en / zh) read "No position holds every picked capability: only people granted them directly will see this view / it". A person's capabilities are the UNION over every set of every position they hold (`resolve-authz-context.ts`, the `boundSets` loop at `:2652-2668` and the `systemPermissions` fold at `:2106-2109`), and the gate asks that union (`holdsRequiredPermissions`). So with two capabilities picked, each granted through a different position, a person holding both positions sees the view or dashboard with no direct grant at all, while the preview tells the administrator that only directly granted people will. The PR's own pin is that case: `viewAudience-34908.test.tsx:213-220` picks `export_reports` (position `sales_rep`) and `view_deal_finance` (positions `sales_lead`, `accountant`) and asserts the exclusive sentence, though a holder of `sales_rep` and `accountant` passes the gate. It holds on all three kinds the sentence appears on (the card's view item, the Studio view row, the dashboard row). The error under-reports who sees the item, the direction an audience control should not err in, though everyone it omits does hold every capability the gate names. Fix: drop the exclusive clause or say what is true, for example "No single position holds every picked capability; people who hold them all between several positions, or by direct grant, will see it", in every copy and the pin. Not measured, and worth a look in the same fix: whether a set every member holds additively (the `everyone` anchor's default sets, when `everyone` is not a row of `/meta/position`) can make the same sentence false with one capability picked.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- N6: `view.switcher.audienceLoadFailed` says "the view can only be shared with everyone" while a gate inherited from the open view stays picked, stays removable and is written on Create (the picker's own docblock says so). In that corner the sentence and the chips above it disagree; it errs toward the stricter outcome and the self-refusal line is shown beside it.
- N7: `engine.form.audienceEveryone` ("everyone who can see the list sees it") is worded for a list view and is also drawn on the dashboard row, whose hint says "everyone sees this dashboard". Readable as the dashboard list the hint itself mentions, so loose, not false; N2 of #37839 already carries the dashboard wording.
- N8: the docblock of `loadCapabilityAudience` in `capabilityAudience.ts` still says the pickers "keep a text box" on a failed read. No picker has one since R4. Comment only.
- N9: `buildCapabilityAudience` keys a set's capabilities by bare name, and `_grantedPermissionSets` carries names only, so two permission sets sharing a name across packages (ADR-0150 D3) fold into one in the advisory preview. Follow-up material; the gate is unaffected.
- N2 to N4 of #37839 stand as recorded there; N5 is closed by this diff (see ①).

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), open on this head.
